title: The Green Door at Five
subtitle: 烘焙与面包店 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 烘焙与面包店（生活与学习·饮食与烹饪）
meta: 主题语境：烘焙与面包店（生活与学习·饮食与烹饪）　|　核心词汇：bakery　|　正文 339 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 bakery 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1954 my grandmother walked nine minutes to ① a bakery that opened at five, and she said the walk was the point and the bread was the excuse. The ② bakery, meaning the shop and not the bread, was run by a man who never learned her name in eleven years; a bakery, she said, is the only shop that sells you the smell before it sells you the thing.

Every ③ bakery in that street closed on a Tuesday, and the ④ bakery on the corner, meaning the one with the green door and not either of those, stayed open through two wars by selling less of everything. A bakery, my mother said, is nine parts flour and one part knowing when the street will be hungry; my grandmother said the flour is the easy half.

My father meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ bakery was the whole of Sunday, meaning the smell in the hallway and not the shop. The ⑥ bakery, meaning the warmth and not any of that, arrived at eleven and was gone by twelve; a bakery, he said, is either a place that sells bread or the hour when a house smells like one. He said the second is the one you miss.

By 1979 the ⑦ bakery had become a window with a queue, and the queue had become an argument about the price of a loaf. The ⑧ bakery of the whole thing, my grandmother wrote in March, was nine years of walking and one closed door; a bakery, she said, is either the shop on the corner or the reason you learned the time. She said the reason is the part that outlives the shop.

The ⑨ bakery I remember is the green door, which was painted white in 1981 and never explained. A ⑩ bakery, my mother said in 1984, is the only business that can be ruined by being improved; every bakery, she said, is a smell that has agreed to look like a trade. She said the smell was never part of the sale.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 面包店；糕饼店
B. n. 面包店（指那家店，与面包相对）
C. 固定搭配：walk to a bakery 走到一家面包店
D. n. 面包店（指街上每一家）
E. n. 面包店（指街角那一家）
F. n. 烘焙；面包香气（指家里的味道）
G. n. 烘焙这件事（抽象：温暖与气味）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a bakery that opened at five
The bakery, meaning the shop and not the bread
bakery was the whole of Sunday
the bakery had become a window with a queue
The bakery of the whole thing
A bakery, my mother said in 1984

answers.why: walk to a bakery 意为“走到一家面包店”，1954 年祖母走九分钟到一家五点开门的面包店。
bakery 意为“面包店”，指那家店而不是面包，由一个十一年来没记住她名字的男人经营。
bakery 指街上每一家面包店，那条街上每一家星期二都关门。
bakery 指街角那一家（绿门那家），它靠什么都少卖一点撑过了两场战争。
bakery 意为“烘焙、面包的香气”，父亲说它是星期天的全部，指的是走廊里的气味而不是那家店。
bakery 为抽象用法，指温暖与气味这件事，十一点来，十二点前就散了。
bakery 意为“面包店”，到 1979 年这个 bakery 成了一个带队伍的窗口。
bakery 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，祖母三月写道，整件事权衡下来是九年的奔走和一扇关掉的门。
bakery 意为“面包店”，我记得的是那扇绿门，它在 1981 年被刷成了白色。
bakery 为抽象总称，母亲说面包店是唯一会因为被改进而毁掉的生意。
